title: Architecture Weekly — September 16, 2026
subtitle: Forum held Wednesday 16 September. Delivery covering 12 to 18 September 2026.

exec_summary.headline: Architecture agreed one way to store service credentials, so rotating one no longer needs a code change.

points.text: Every brand moves its service credentials to the managed store. Teams stop keeping their own copies, so a rotation is an operations task instead of a release.
The new US brand's non-prod network went live, and the Claude and Snowflake tooling picked up three more deliveries.
Two teams have not named a migration date. Architecture is chasing both and will report next week.

exec_summary.footer: No decision is waiting on leadership this week.

objective: Agree a single way to store and rotate service credentials across the brands.

outcome.text: The group agreed the managed store, and a named owner is running the rollout.

tldr: One store for every brand, no code change to rotate a credential, and the rollout starts next sprint.

decisions.lead: Service credentials move to the managed store.
decisions.text: Every brand reads from it at run time instead of holding its own copy.
decisions.rationale: Rotation needs no code change and no key manifest, so an expired credential stops being a release-blocking incident.

decisions.text: The group kept the manual path for now and will revisit once the store is in production.
decisions.rationale: Automating it before the store carries real traffic would add a second untested path to the same problem.

actions.action: Confirm a migration date for the two remaining teams.
Write the rotation runbook and put it through review.

topics.title: Credential storage.
topics.summary: Two options were compared against rotation cost. The managed store won on operations, not on price.

topics.title: Break-glass access.
topics.summary: The group wants an automated path but not before the store is proven in production.

topics.title: Migration sequencing.
topics.summary: Two teams have not given a date. Architecture is following up outside the forum.

open_questions: Who owns the break-glass path once the managed store carries production traffic?
What is the rollback position if a brand cannot migrate inside the agreed window?
artifacts: Credential rotation design note. Screen-shared; file name not stated.
Platform runbook index. Referenced by name only.
speakers: Alexandre Castro, Platform lead, Security lead

items.sentence: The new US brand's non-prod network went live and is carrying traffic.
Snowflake cost reporting now refreshes on its own every morning.
Architecture published the credential rotation standard for review.
